saw_lines: Appliance buyers compare two or three models on price and delivery, then need one reason to pick today.
So the sale is decided in the opening line, where a buyer needs a proof number and one reason to act.
Your 25 copy ads carry no proof number, so pick one real figure, like your review count or orders shipped, and lead the next batch with it.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 27 Oct 2026
points: None of your 25 copy ads carries a proof number, so a new buyer has nothing concrete to trust before the click. Pick one real figure, like your review count or orders shipped, and open the next batch with it.
None of your 25 copy ads names an offer, so a new buyer has no reason to act today. Open three new ads with a first order offer and a clear end date, then test them against the current copy.

Your 25 copy ads open with 13 different stories, and the biggest leads only 4 ads, so no hook gets enough repetition to learn from. Pick the two strongest stories and build the next batch from them, three variations each.

17 of your ads have stayed live for 60 days or more, so the core idea has earned its place. Build three more variations on the oldest one, each with a new first line, before the same audience sees it too often.
